verses.1:1: Now it came to pass after the death of Joshua that the children of Israel inquired of the LORD, saying, "Who shall go up first for us against the Canaanites to fight against them?"
verses.1:2: And the LORD said, "Judah shall go up. Behold, I have given the land into his hand."
verses.1:3: Then Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Go up with me into my lot, and let us fight against the Canaanites; and I also will go with you into your lot." So Simeon went with him.
verses.1:4: And Judah went up, and the LORD delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand; and they struck them down at Bezek, ten thousand men.
verses.1:5: And they found Adoni-Bezek in Bezek and fought against him, and they struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
verses.1:6: But Adoni-Bezek fled, and they pursued him and captured him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
verses.1:7: And Adoni-Bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and their big toes cut off used to glean beneath my table; just as I have done, so God has repaid me." And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
verses.1:8: Now the children of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it; they struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.
verses.1:9: And afterward the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who dwelt in the hill country, the Negev, and the lowland.
verses.1:10: Then Judah marched against the Canaanites who dwelt in Hebron—now the name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath Arba—and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
verses.1:11: From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir; now the name of Debir formerly was Kiriath Sepher.
verses.1:12: And Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath Sepher and captures it, to him I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife."
verses.1:13: And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it; so he gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
verses.1:14: Now it came to pass, when she came, that she urged him to ask of her father a field. Then she dismounted from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you wish?"
verses.1:15: And she said to him, "Give me a blessing; since you have given me the land of the Negev, give me also springs of water." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
verses.1:16: Now the children of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up from the City of Palms with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which lies in the Negev of Arad; and they went and dwelt with the people.
verses.1:17: Then Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath and devoted it to destruction. Therefore the name of the city was called Hormah.
verses.1:18: Also Judah captured Gaza with its territory, Ashkelon with its territory, and Ekron with its territory.
verses.1:19: And the LORD was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country; yet he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
verses.1:20: And they gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had spoken; and from there he drove out the three sons of Anak.
verses.1:21: But the children of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem; so the Jebusites have dwelt with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.1:22: And the house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
verses.1:23: So the house of Joseph scouted out Bethel; now the name of the city formerly was Luz.
verses.1:24: And the watchmen saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, "Please show us the entrance to the city, and we will show mercy to you."
verses.1:25: So he showed them the entrance to the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but the man and all his family they let go.
verses.1:26: And the man went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day.
verses.1:27: Manasseh did not dispossess Beth Shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, or the inhabitants of Ibleam and its villages, or the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages; for the Canaanites persisted in dwelling in that land.
verses.1:28: And it came to pass, when Israel grew strong, that they put the Canaanites to forced labor, yet did not completely drive them out.
verses.1:29: Nor did Ephraim drive out the Canaanites who dwelt in Gezer; so the Canaanites dwelt in their midst in Gezer.
verses.1:30: Zebulun did not drive out the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol; so the Canaanites dwelt in their midst and became subject to forced labor.
verses.1:31: Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
verses.1:32: So the Asherites dwelt in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; for they did not drive them out.
verses.1:33: Naphtali did not drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth Anath, but dwelt in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh and Beth Anath became subject to forced labor for them.
verses.1:34: And the Amorites pressed the children of Dan into the hill country, for they would not allow them to come down into the valley.
verses.1:35: And the Amorites persisted in dwelling in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim; yet the hand of the house of Joseph grew heavy, and they became subject to forced labor.
verses.1:36: Now the border of the Amorites was from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela, and upward.
verses.2:1: Then the Angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you up from Egypt and led you into the land which I swore to your fathers; and I said, 'I will never break My covenant with you.
verses.2:2: And you shall make no covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you shall tear down their altars.' Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this that you have done?
verses.2:3: Therefore I also said, 'I will not drive them out from before you; rather, they shall be adversaries to you, and their gods shall be a snare to you.'"
verses.2:4: And it came to pass, when the Angel of the LORD spoke these words to all the children of Israel, that the people lifted up their voice and wept.
verses.2:5: So they called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
verses.2:6: When Joshua dismissed the people, the children of Israel went each man to his inheritance to possess the land.
verses.2:7: So the people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work of the LORD which He had done for Israel.
verses.2:8: Now Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died, being one hundred and ten years old.
verses.2:9: And they buried him within the border of his inheritance at Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north side of Mount Gaash.
verses.2:10: Also all that generation were gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know the LORD, nor the work which He had done for Israel.
verses.2:11: Then the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD, and served the Baals;
verses.2:12: and they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt; and they went after other gods from among the gods of the peoples who were all around them, and they bowed down to them; and they provoked the LORD to anger.
verses.2:13: They forsook the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
verses.2:14: And the anger of the LORD burned against Israel. So He delivered them into the hand of plunderers who plundered them; and He sold them into the hand of their enemies all around, so that they could no longer stand before their enemies.
verses.2:15: Wherever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for calamity, as the LORD had spoken and as the LORD had sworn to them; and they were greatly distressed.
verses.2:16: Nevertheless, the LORD raised up judges who delivered them out of the hand of those who plundered them.
verses.2:17: Yet they would not listen to their judges either, for they played the harlot after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers had walked, in obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not do so.
verses.2:18: And whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and delivered them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning because of those who oppressed them and afflicted them.
verses.2:19: And it came to pass, when the judge died, that they would turn back and act more corruptly than their fathers, by going after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They did not abandon their practices nor their stubborn way.
verses.2:20: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He said, "Because this nation has transgressed My covenant which I commanded their fathers, and has not obeyed My voice,
verses.2:21: I also will no longer drive out before them any of the nations which Joshua left when he died,
verses.2:22: so that through them I may test Israel, whether they will keep the way of the LORD to walk in it, just as their fathers kept it, or not."
verses.2:23: Therefore the LORD left those nations, without driving them out hastily; nor did He deliver them into the hand of Joshua.
verses.3:1: Now these are the nations that the LORD left remaining to test Israel by them—all those who had not known any of the wars of Canaan,
verses.3:2: only so that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them warfare, at least those who beforehand had not known them:
verses.3:3: the five lords of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites dwelling in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon as far as the entrance of Hamath.
verses.3:4: And they were there to test Israel by them, to know whether they would heed the commandments of the LORD, which He had commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
verses.3:5: So the children of Israel dwelt in the midst of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.3:6: And they took their daughters to themselves for wives, and gave their own daughters to their sons; and they served their gods.
verses.3:7: Then the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD, and they forgot the LORD their God, and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
verses.3:8: Therefore the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram Naharaim; and the children of Israel served Cushan-Rishathaim eight years.
verses.3:9: When the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for the children of Israel who delivered them—Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
verses.3:10: And the Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD delivered Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed against Cushan-Rishathaim.
verses.3:11: So the land had rest forty years. Then Othniel the son of Kenaz died.
verses.3:12: And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD; and the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the LORD.
verses.3:13: And he gathered to himself the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the City of Palms.
verses.3:14: So the children of Israel served Eglon king of Moab eighteen years.
verses.3:15: But when the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. And by his hand the children of Israel sent tribute to Eglon king of Moab.
verses.3:16: Now Ehud made for himself a double-edged sword, a cubit in length, and girded it under his garments on his right thigh.
verses.3:17: And he presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
verses.3:18: And it came to pass, when he had finished presenting the tribute, that he sent away the people who had carried the tribute.
verses.3:19: But he himself turned back from the carved images that were near Gilgal, and said, "I have a secret message for you, O king." And he said, "Keep silence!" So all who attended him went out from his presence.
verses.3:20: Then Ehud came to him while he was sitting in the cool upper chamber that belonged to him alone. And Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." So he arose from his seat.
verses.3:21: And Ehud reached out with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly.
verses.3:22: Even the hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not draw the sword out of his belly; and the dung came out.
verses.3:23: Then Ehud went out onto the porch, and shut the doors of the upper chamber behind him and locked them.
verses.3:24: When Ehud had gone out, Eglon's servants came and looked, and behold, the doors of the upper chamber were locked. So they said, "Surely he is covering his feet in the cool chamber."
verses.3:25: So they waited until they were embarrassed; and behold, he still did not open the doors of the upper chamber. Therefore they took the key and opened them, and behold, their master lay fallen on the floor, dead.
verses.3:26: Meanwhile Ehud had escaped while they delayed, and he passed beyond the carved images and escaped to Seirah.
verses.3:27: And it came to pass, when he arrived, that he blew the trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the children of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he went before them.
verses.3:28: Then he said to them, "Follow after me, for the LORD has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand." So they went down after him, seized the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and did not allow anyone to cross over.
verses.3:29: And at that time they struck down about ten thousand men of Moab, every robust man and every man of valor; and not a man escaped.
verses.3:30: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest eighty years.
verses.3:31: After him was Shamgar the son of Anath, who struck down six hundred men of the Philistines with an oxgoad; and he also delivered Israel.
verses.4:1: And the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, now that Ehud was dead.
verses.4:2: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who dwelt in Harosheth Hagoyim.
verses.4:3: And the children of Israel cried out to the LORD; for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he harshly oppressed the children of Israel for twenty years.
verses.4:4: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
verses.4:5: And she would sit beneath the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.
verses.4:6: Then she sent and summoned Barak the son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, and said to him, "Has not the LORD God of Israel commanded, 'Go and march to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the sons of Naphtali and of the sons of Zebulun;
verses.4:7: and I will draw out to you, at the Brook Kishon, Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand'?"
verses.4:8: And Barak said to her, "If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go."
verses.4:9: And she said, "I will surely go with you; nevertheless, the glory will not be yours on the way that you are going, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." Then Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
verses.4:10: And Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; and ten thousand men went up at his heels, and Deborah went up with him.
verses.4:11: Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites, from the descendants of Hobab the father-in-law of Moses, and had pitched his tent as far as the terebinth tree in Zaanannim, which is near Kedesh.
verses.4:12: And they reported to Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
verses.4:13: So Sisera summoned all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth Hagoyim to the Brook Kishon.
verses.4:14: Then Deborah said to Barak, "Arise! For this is the day in which the LORD has delivered Sisera into your hand. Has not the LORD gone out before you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men following him.
verses.4:15: And the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera alighted from his chariot and fled away on foot.
verses.4:16: But Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth Hagoyim, and all the army of Sisera fell by the edge of the sword; not even one was left.
verses.4:17: However, Sisera had fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.
verses.4:18: And Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not be afraid." So he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
verses.4:19: Then he said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." So she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him.
verses.4:20: And he said to her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if any man comes and asks you, saying, 'Is there any man here?' then you shall say, 'No.'"
verses.4:21: Then Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly to him and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground; for he was fast asleep and exhausted. So he died.
verses.4:22: And behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him and said to him, "Come, and I will show you the man whom you are seeking." And he went in with her, and behold, Sisera lay dead, with the peg in his temple.
verses.4:23: So on that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the children of Israel.
verses.4:24: And the hand of the children of Israel pressed ever harder against Jabin king of Canaan, until they had cut off Jabin king of Canaan.
verses.5:1: Then Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying:
verses.5:2: "When leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people offered themselves willingly, bless the LORD!
verses.5:3: Hear, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I, even I, will sing to the LORD; I will make melody to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.5:4: O LORD, when You went forth from Seir, when You marched from the field of Edom, the earth trembled, and the heavens also dripped; yes, the clouds dripped with water.
verses.5:5: The mountains flowed before the LORD, even Sinai before the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.5:6: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted, and travelers kept to winding byways.
verses.5:7: Village life ceased in Israel, it ceased, until I, Deborah, arose, until I arose as a mother in Israel.
verses.5:8: They chose new gods; then war was at the gates. Not a shield or a spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.
verses.5:9: My heart goes out to the commanders of Israel, who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless the LORD!
verses.5:10: Speak forth, you who ride on white donkeys, who sit upon rich carpets, and who walk along the road.
verses.5:11: Far from the clamor of archers among the watering places, there they shall rehearse the righteous deeds of the LORD, the righteous deeds for His villagers in Israel; then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
verses.5:12: Awake, awake, Deborah! Awake, awake, utter a song! Arise, Barak, and lead away your captives, O son of Abinoam!
verses.5:13: Then the remnant marched down against the nobles of the people; the LORD marched down for me against the mighty.
verses.5:14: Out of Ephraim came those whose root is in Amalek, after you, Benjamin, among your peoples; from Machir commanders marched down, and from Zebulun those who bear the marshal's staff.
verses.5:15: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; and as was Issachar, so was Barak, sent forth into the valley at his heels. Among the divisions of Reuben there were great resolves of heart.
verses.5:16: Why did you linger among the sheepfolds, to hear the piping for the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben there were great searchings of heart.
verses.5:17: Gilead abode beyond the Jordan; and why did Dan tarry with the ships? Asher sat still along the seashore and dwelt by his inlets.
verses.5:18: Zebulun is a people who scorned their lives even to death, and Naphtali also, upon the heights of the field.
verses.5:19: The kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo; they took no spoils of silver.
verses.5:20: From the heavens they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
verses.5:21: The torrent of Kishon swept them away, that ancient torrent, the torrent of Kishon. March on, O my soul, in strength!
verses.5:22: Then the hooves of the horses hammered, with the galloping, the galloping of his mighty steeds.
verses.5:23: 'Curse Meroz,' said the Angel of the LORD, 'bitterly curse its inhabitants, because they did not come to the help of the LORD, to the help of the LORD against the mighty.'
verses.5:24: Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; blessed is she above women in the tent.
verses.5:25: He asked for water, and she gave him milk; in a lordly bowl she brought forth curds.
verses.5:26: She put her hand to the tent peg, and her right hand to the hammer of the workmen; she struck Sisera, she crushed his head, and she shattered and pierced through his temple.
verses.5:27: Between her feet he sank, he fell, he lay still; between her feet he sank, he fell; where he sank, there he fell slain.
verses.5:28: Through the window she looked out and cried aloud, the mother of Sisera through the lattice: 'Why does his chariot delay in coming? Why do the hoofbeats of his chariots tarry?'
verses.5:29: Her wisest ladies answer her; indeed, she repeats her own words to herself:
verses.5:30: 'Are they not finding and dividing the spoil: a maiden or two for every warrior, spoil of dyed garments for Sisera, spoil of dyed embroidered garments, a dyed cloth doubly embroidered for the necks of the spoil?'
verses.5:31: Thus let all Your enemies perish, O LORD! Yet let those who love Him be as the sun going forth in its might." And the land had rest forty years.
verses.6:1: Then the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD delivered them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
verses.6:2: And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel; because of Midian, the children of Israel made for themselves the dens that are in the mountains, and the caves, and the strongholds.
verses.6:3: And whenever Israel had sown, Midian would come up, together with Amalek and the people of the East; indeed, they would come up against them.
verses.6:4: They would encamp against them and destroy the produce of the earth as far as Gaza, and leave no sustenance in Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor donkey.
verses.6:5: For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, and they would come as numerous as locusts; both they and their camels were without number, and they entered the land to devastate it.
verses.6:6: So Israel was greatly impoverished because of Midian, and the children of Israel cried out to the LORD.
verses.6:7: And it came to pass, when the children of Israel cried out to the LORD on account of Midian,
verses.6:8: that the LORD sent a prophet to the children of Israel, who said to them, "Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out of the house of bondage;
verses.6:9: and I delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of all who oppressed you, and drove them out from before you and gave you their land.
verses.6:10: And I said to you, 'I am the LORD your God; you shall not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell.' Yet you have not obeyed My voice."
verses.6:11: Now the Angel of the LORD came and sat under the terebinth tree that was in Ophrah, which belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while his son Gideon was beating out wheat in the winepress to hide it from Midian.
verses.6:12: And the Angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, "The LORD is with you, you mighty man of valor!"
verses.6:13: And Gideon said to Him, "O my lord, if the LORD is with us, why then has all this befallen us? And where are all His wondrous deeds of which our fathers told us, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' Yet now the LORD has forsaken us and delivered us into the hand of Midian."
verses.6:14: Then the LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this might of yours, and you shall save Israel from the hand of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
verses.6:15: So he said to Him, "O my Lord, how can I save Israel? Behold, my clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house."
verses.6:16: And the LORD said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you shall strike down Midian as one man."
verses.6:17: Then he said to Him, "If now I have found favor in Your sight, then show me a sign that it is You who speak with me.
verses.6:18: Do not depart from here, I pray, until I come to You and bring out my offering and set it before You." And He said, "I will wait until you return."
verses.6:19: So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat, and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour; the meat he put in a basket, and the broth he put in a pot, and he brought them out to Him under the terebinth tree and presented them.
verses.6:20: And the Angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened cakes and lay them upon this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.
verses.6:21: Then the Angel of the LORD put forth the tip of the staff that was in His hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire rose up out of the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes. And the Angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
verses.6:22: And Gideon perceived that He was the Angel of the LORD. So Gideon said, "Alas, O Lord GOD! For I have seen the Angel of the LORD face to face!"
verses.6:23: Then the LORD said to him, "Peace be to you; do not fear, you shall not die."
verses.6:24: So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD, and called it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
verses.6:25: And it came to pass on that same night that the LORD said to him, "Take your father's young bull, and the second bull of seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it;
verses.6:26: and build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold in proper order, and take the second bull and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah which you shall cut down."
verses.6:27: Then Gideon took ten men from among his servants and did as the LORD had spoken to him. Yet because he feared his father's household and the men of the city too much to do it by day, he did it by night.
verses.6:28: And when the men of the city arose early in the morning, behold, the altar of Baal was torn down, and the Asherah that was beside it was cut down, and the second bull was offered upon the altar that had been built.
verses.6:29: So they said to one another, "Who has done this thing?" And when they inquired and asked, they said, "Gideon the son of Joash has done this thing."
verses.6:30: Then the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son, that he may die, because he has torn down the altar of Baal, and because he has cut down the Asherah that was beside it."
verses.6:31: But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Will you contend for Baal? Or will you save him? Whoever contends for him shall be put to death by morning! If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because he has torn down his altar!"
verses.6:32: Therefore on that day he called him Jerubbaal, saying, "Let Baal contend against him, because he has torn down his altar."
verses.6:33: Then all Midian and Amalek and the people of the East gathered together; and they crossed over and encamped in the Valley of Jezreel.
verses.6:34: But the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon; and he blew the trumpet, and the Abiezrites were summoned behind him.
verses.6:35: And he sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, who also were summoned behind him; and he sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
verses.6:36: Then Gideon said to God, "If You will save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken,
verses.6:37: behold, I am placing a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if there is dew on the fleece alone, and dryness upon all the ground, then I shall know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken."
verses.6:38: And it was so. When he arose early the next morning and squeezed the fleece, he wrung out dew from the fleece, a bowl full of water.
verses.6:39: Then Gideon said to God, "Do not let Your anger burn against me, and let me speak but this once; let me test, I pray, just this once with the fleece; let dryness be upon the fleece alone, and upon all the ground let there be dew."
verses.6:40: And God did so that night; for there was dryness upon the fleece alone, and upon all the ground there was dew.
verses.7:1: Then Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—and all the people who were with him rose early and encamped beside the spring of Harod; and the camp of Midian lay to the north of them, by the hill of Moreh in the valley.
verses.7:2: And the LORD said to Gideon, "The people who are with you are too many for Me to give Midian into their hand, lest Israel boast against Me, saying, 'My own hand has delivered me.'
verses.7:3: Now therefore, proclaim in the hearing of the people, saying, 'Whoever is fearful and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.'" And twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, while ten thousand remained.
verses.7:4: Then the LORD said to Gideon, "The people are still too many; bring them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. And it shall be that of whom I say to you, 'This one shall go with you,' the same shall go with you; and of every one of whom I say to you, 'This one shall not go with you,' the same shall not go."
verses.7:5: So he brought the people down to the water. And the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps from the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you shall set apart by himself; likewise everyone who kneels down upon his knees to drink."
verses.7:6: And the number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people knelt down upon their knees to drink water.
verses.7:7: Then the LORD said to Gideon, "By the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and I will deliver Midian into your hand; let all the people go, every man to his own place."
verses.7:8: So they took the people's provisions in their hands, and their trumpets; and he sent away all the men of Israel, every man to his tents, but retained the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian was below him in the valley.
verses.7:9: And it came to pass that same night that the LORD said to him, "Arise, go down against the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand.
verses.7:10: Yet if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant,
verses.7:11: and you shall hear what they speak; and afterward your hands shall be strengthened, and you shall go down against the camp." Then he went down, he and Purah his servant, to the outpost of the armed men who were in the camp.
verses.7:12: Now Midian and Amalek and all the sons of the East lay in the valley like locusts in multitude, and their camels were beyond number, like the sand upon the seashore in multitude.
verses.7:13: And when Gideon arrived, behold, a man was relating a dream to his companion; and he said, "Behold, I have dreamed a dream, and behold, a loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian; it reached the tent and struck it so that it fell, and overturned it upside down, and the tent fell."
verses.7:14: Then his companion answered and said, "This is nothing else but the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel! Into his hand God has delivered Midian and all the camp."
verses.7:15: And it came to pass, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he worshiped. Then he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for the LORD has delivered into your hand the camp of Midian."
verses.7:16: And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put trumpets into the hands of all of them, along with empty pitchers and torches within the pitchers.
verses.7:17: And he said to them, "Watch me and do likewise; behold, when I come to the edge of the camp, it shall be that as I do, so you shall do.
verses.7:18: When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then you also shall blow the trumpets all around the entire camp and say, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"
verses.7:19: So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, when they had just posted the watchmen; and they blew the trumpets and shattered the pitchers that were in their hands.
verses.7:20: Then the three companies blew the trumpets and broke the pitchers; they held the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands for blowing, and they cried out, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
verses.7:21: And every man stood in his place all around the camp; and all the camp ran, and shouted aloud, and fled.
verses.7:22: When they blew the three hundred trumpets, the LORD set every man's sword against his companion throughout the whole camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel Meholah by Tabbath.
verses.7:23: And the men of Israel were summoned from Naphtali, from Asher, and from all Manasseh, and they pursued after Midian.
verses.7:24: And Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against Midian, and seize the waters before them as far as Beth Barah, and the Jordan." So all the men of Ephraim were summoned, and they seized the waters as far as Beth Barah, and the Jordan.
verses.7:25: And they captured the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; they slew Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb they slew at the winepress of Zeeb. Then they pursued Midian, and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan.
verses.8:1: Now the men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this thing that you have done to us, not to call us when you went to fight against Midian?" And they contended with him sharply.
verses.8:2: So he said to them, "What have I done now in comparison with you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?
verses.8:3: Into your hands God has delivered the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and what was I able to do in comparison with you?" Then their anger toward him subsided when he spoke this word.
verses.8:4: And Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men who were with him, weary yet still pursuing.
verses.8:5: Then he said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me, for they are weary, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, kings of Midian."
verses.8:6: And the officials of Succoth said, "Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?"
verses.8:7: So Gideon said, "Therefore, when the LORD has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers."
verses.8:8: And he went up from there to Penuel and spoke to them in the same manner; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
verses.8:9: So he spoke also to the men of Penuel, saying, "When I return in peace, I will tear down this tower."
verses.8:10: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were at Karkor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand men—all who were left of all the army of the sons of the East; for those who had fallen were one hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.8:11: Then Gideon went up by the way of those who dwell in tents, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he struck the camp while the camp felt secure.
verses.8:12: And Zebah and Zalmunna fled, and he pursued after them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the entire camp into panic.
verses.8:13: Then Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle by the Ascent of Heres.
verses.8:14: And he captured a young man from the men of Succoth and questioned him; and he wrote down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.
verses.8:15: Then he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Behold Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you taunted me, saying, 'Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your hand, that we should give bread to your weary men?'"
verses.8:16: And he took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth a lesson.
verses.8:17: And he tore down the tower of Penuel and slew the men of the city.
verses.8:18: Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "What manner of men were they whom you slew at Tabor?" And they answered, "As you are, so were they; every one resembled the sons of a king."
verses.8:19: And he said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not slay you."
verses.8:20: Then he said to Jether his firstborn, "Arise, slay them!" But the youth did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, because he was still a youth.
verses.8:21: So Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Rise up yourself and strike us down, for as a man is, so is his strength." Then Gideon arose and slew Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:22: Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, both you and your son, and your son's son as well; for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian."
verses.8:23: But Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, nor shall my son rule over you; the LORD shall rule over you."
verses.8:24: Then Gideon said to them, "Let me make a request of you, that every man give me an earring from his spoil"—for they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
verses.8:25: And they answered, "We will gladly give them." So they spread out a garment, and every man cast upon it an earring from his spoil.
verses.8:26: And the weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescent ornaments, the pendants, and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that were around the necks of their camels.
verses.8:27: And Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, in Ophrah; and all Israel played the harlot after it there, and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.
verses.8:28: Thus Midian was subdued before the children of Israel, and they did not lift up their heads again; and the land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.
verses.8:29: Then Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and dwelt in his own house.
verses.8:30: Now Gideon had seventy sons who came from his loins, for he had many wives.
verses.8:31: And his concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he gave him the name Abimelech.
verses.8:32: And Gideon the son of Joash died in a good old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
verses.8:33: And it came to pass, as soon as Gideon was dead, that the children of Israel turned again and played the harlot after the Baals, and made Baal Berith their god.
verses.8:34: And the children of Israel did not remember the LORD their God, who had delivered them from the hand of all their enemies on every side;
verses.8:35: nor did they show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal—that is, Gideon—according to all the good that he had done for Israel.
verses.9:1: Now Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and spoke with them and with all the family of the house of his mother's father, saying,
verses.9:2: "Please speak in the hearing of all the lords of Shechem: 'Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you?' And remember that I am your bone and your flesh."
verses.9:3: So his mother's brothers spoke all these words concerning him in the hearing of all the lords of Shechem; and their heart inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
verses.9:4: And they gave him seventy pieces of silver from the house of Baal-Berith, with which Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, and they followed him.
verses.9:5: Then he came to his father's house at Ophrah and slew his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, upon one stone. Yet Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left, for he had hidden himself.
verses.9:6: And all the lords of Shechem and all Beth-Millo gathered together, and they went and made Abimelech king beside the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.
verses.9:7: When they told Jotham, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, and lifted up his voice and cried out, and said to them, "Listen to me, you lords of Shechem, that God may listen to you!
verses.9:8: Once the trees went forth to anoint a king over themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us!'
verses.9:9: But the olive tree said to them, 'Shall I leave my rich oil, by which God and men are honored, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:10: Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'You come and reign over us!'
verses.9:11: But the fig tree said to them, 'Shall I leave my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:12: Then the trees said to the vine, 'You come and reign over us!'
verses.9:13: And the vine said to them, 'Shall I leave my new wine, which cheers God and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:14: Then all the trees said to the bramble, 'You come and reign over us!'
verses.9:15: And the bramble said to the trees, 'If in truth you are anointing me as king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; but if not, let fire come forth from the bramble and devour the cedars of Lebanon!'
verses.9:16: Now therefore, if you have acted in truth and integrity in making Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done to him as his hands deserved—
verses.9:17: for my father fought for you, and risked his life, and delivered you from the hand of Midian;
verses.9:18: yet you have risen up against my father's house this day and slain his sons, seventy men, upon one stone, and made Abimelech, the son of his maidservant, king over the lords of Shechem, because he is your brother—
verses.9:19: if then you have acted in truth and integrity with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.
verses.9:20: But if not, let fire come forth from Abimelech and devour the lords of Shechem and Beth-Millo; and let fire come forth from the lords of Shechem and from Beth-Millo and devour Abimelech!"
verses.9:21: Then Jotham ran away and fled, and went to Beer and dwelt there, because of Abimelech his brother.
verses.9:22: Now Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.
verses.9:23: Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem; and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,
verses.9:24: that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, who slew them, and upon the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to slay his brothers.
verses.9:25: And the lords of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who passed by them along that way; and it was told to Abimelech.
verses.9:26: Now Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brothers and crossed over into Shechem; and the lords of Shechem put their confidence in him.
verses.9:27: So they went out into the fields, and gathered the grapes of their vineyards and trod them, and held a festival; and they went into the house of their god, and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.
verses.9:28: Then Gaal the son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is Zebul not his officer? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why then should we serve him?
verses.9:29: Would that this people were under my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech." So he said to Abimelech, "Increase your army and come out!"
verses.9:30: When Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger was kindled.
verses.9:31: And he sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, "Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and behold, they are stirring up the city against you.
verses.9:32: Now therefore, arise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in wait in the field.
verses.9:33: And it shall be in the morning, as soon as the sun rises, that you shall rise early and rush upon the city; and behold, when he and the people who are with him come out against you, you may do to him whatever your hand finds to do."
verses.9:34: So Abimelech and all the people who were with him arose by night, and they lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
verses.9:35: Now Gaal the son of Ebed went out and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city; and Abimelech and the people who were with him rose up from the ambush.
verses.9:36: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, "Behold, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains!" But Zebul said to him, "You see the shadow of the mountains as if they were men."
verses.9:37: And Gaal spoke yet again and said, "Behold, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Oak of the Diviners."
verses.9:38: Then Zebul said to him, "Where indeed is your mouth now, with which you said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is this not the people whom you despised? Come, go out now and fight against them!"
verses.9:39: So Gaal went out before the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
verses.9:40: And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him; and many fell slain, even up to the entrance of the gate.
verses.9:41: Then Abimelech dwelt at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers, so that they could not dwell in Shechem.
verses.9:42: And it came to pass on the next day that the people went out into the field, and they told Abimelech.
verses.9:43: So he took the people, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the field; and he looked, and behold, the people were coming out of the city, and he rose up against them and struck them down.
verses.9:44: And Abimelech and the companies that were with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city; and the two companies rushed upon all who were in the field and struck them down.
verses.9:45: So Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he captured the city and slew the people who were in it, and he tore down the city and sowed it with salt.
verses.9:46: Now when all the lords of the tower of Shechem heard of it, they entered the stronghold of the house of El-Berith.
verses.9:47: And it was told to Abimelech that all the lords of the tower of Shechem were gathered together.
verses.9:48: Then Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took an axe in his hand and cut down a bough from the trees, and lifted it and laid it on his shoulder, and said to the people who were with him, "What you have seen me do, make haste and do likewise!"
verses.9:49: So every man among all the people likewise cut down his bough and followed Abimelech, and laid them against the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire over them; so all the people of the tower of Shechem also died, about a thousand men and women.
verses.9:50: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, and encamped against Thebez and captured it.
verses.9:51: But there was a strong tower in the midst of the city, and all the men and women and all the lords of the city fled there and shut themselves in; and they went up to the roof of the tower.
verses.9:52: So Abimelech came up to the tower and fought against it; and he drew near to the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
verses.9:53: And a certain woman cast an upper millstone upon Abimelech's head and crushed his skull.
verses.9:54: Then he called hastily to the young man, his armor-bearer, and said to him, "Draw your sword and slay me, lest men say of me, 'A woman slew him.'" So his young man thrust him through, and he died.
verses.9:55: And when the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, every man departed to his own place.
verses.9:56: Thus God repaid the wickedness of Abimelech, which he had done to his father in slaying his seventy brothers.
verses.9:57: And all the wickedness of the men of Shechem God returned upon their own heads, and upon them came the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal.
verses.10:1: After Abimelech, there arose to save Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he dwelt in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.10:2: He judged Israel twenty-three years; then he died and was buried in Shamir.
verses.10:3: And after him arose Jair the Gileadite, and he judged Israel twenty-two years.
verses.10:4: Now he had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts, and they had thirty towns—which are called Havoth Jair to this day—that are in the land of Gilead.
verses.10:5: And Jair died and was buried in Kamon.
verses.10:6: Then the children of Israel again did evil in the sight of the LORD, and served the Baals and the Ashtoreths, and the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines; and they forsook the LORD and did not serve Him.
verses.10:7: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the children of Ammon.
verses.10:8: And they shattered and crushed the children of Israel in that year—for eighteen years—all the children of Israel who were beyond the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
verses.10:9: Moreover, the children of Ammon crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah also, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was greatly distressed.
verses.10:10: Then the children of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, "We have sinned against You, for we have forsaken our God and have served the Baals."
verses.10:11: And the LORD said to the children of Israel, "Did I not deliver you from Egypt, and from the Amorites, and from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?
verses.10:12: The Sidonians also, and Amalek, and Maon oppressed you; and you cried out to Me, and I saved you out of their hand.
verses.10:13: Yet you have forsaken Me and served other gods; therefore I will save you no more.
verses.10:14: Go and cry out to the gods whom you have chosen; let them save you in the time of your distress."
verses.10:15: And the children of Israel said to the LORD, "We have sinned! Do to us according to all that is good in Your sight; only deliver us, we pray, this day."
verses.10:16: So they put away the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD; and His soul could no longer endure the misery of Israel.
verses.10:17: Then the children of Ammon were summoned together and encamped in Gilead; and the children of Israel assembled themselves and encamped in Mizpah.
verses.10:18: And the people, the leaders of Gilead, said one to another, "Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
verses.11:1: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor, and he was the son of a harlot; and Gilead fathered Jephthah.
verses.11:2: Now Gilead's wife bore sons to him; and when the sons of the wife grew up, they cast Jephthah out and said to him, "You shall not inherit in our father's house, for you are the son of another woman."
verses.11:3: Then Jephthah fled from his brethren and dwelt in the land of Tob; and worthless men gathered to Jephthah and went out with him.
verses.11:4: And it came to pass after some time that the children of Ammon made war against Israel.
verses.11:5: And so it was, when the children of Ammon made war against Israel, that the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.
verses.11:6: And they said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, that we may fight against the children of Ammon."
verses.11:7: So Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Did you not hate me and drive me out from my father's house? Why then have you come to me now when you are in distress?"
verses.11:8: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "For this reason we have turned back to you now, that you may go with us and fight against the children of Ammon, and become head over us—over all the inhabitants of Gilead."
verses.11:9: Then Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD delivers them before me, then I shall be your head."
verses.11:10: And the elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "The LORD be witness between us if we do not do according to your word."
verses.11:11: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over them as head and commander; and Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD in Mizpah.
verses.11:12: Now Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, "What is there between you and me, that you have come against me to fight in my land?"
verses.11:13: And the king of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Jephthah, "Because Israel took away my land when they came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan. Now therefore, restore them in peace."
verses.11:14: Then Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the children of Ammon,
verses.11:15: and said to him, "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon.
verses.11:16: For when they came up from Egypt, Israel walked through the wilderness to the Red Sea and came to Kadesh.
verses.11:17: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Let me pass, I pray, through your land.' But the king of Edom would not listen. And they sent also to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel remained in Kadesh.
verses.11:18: Then they journeyed through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east side of the land of Moab, and encamped on the other side of the Arnon; yet they did not enter the border of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.
verses.11:19: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land to my place.'
verses.11:20: But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. So Sihon gathered all his people together, and they encamped in Jahaz, and he fought against Israel.
verses.11:21: And the LORD God of Israel delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they defeated them. Thus Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that land.
verses.11:22: So they possessed all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness even to the Jordan.
verses.11:23: And now the LORD God of Israel has dispossessed the Amorites from before His people Israel; and should you possess it?
verses.11:24: Will you not possess whatever Chemosh your god gives you to possess? So whatever the LORD our God has dispossessed from before us, that we will possess.
verses.11:25: And now, are you indeed any better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them?
verses.11:26: While Israel dwelt in Heshbon and its villages, in Aroer and its villages, and in all the cities along the banks of the Arnon for three hundred years, why did you not recover them within that time?
verses.11:27: Therefore I have not sinned against you, yet you are doing me wrong by making war against me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon."
verses.11:28: However, the king of the children of Ammon did not heed the words of Jephthah which he sent to him.
verses.11:29: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, and passed through Mizpeh of Gilead; and from Mizpeh of Gilead he advanced toward the children of Ammon.
verses.11:30: And Jephthah made a vow to the LORD, and said, "If You will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand,
verses.11:31: then it shall be that whatever comes forth from the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the children of Ammon shall surely belong to the LORD, and I will offer it up as a burnt offering."
verses.11:32: So Jephthah crossed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD delivered them into his hand.
verses.11:33: And he struck them from Aroer as far as Minnith—twenty cities—and as far as Abel Keramim, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.
verses.11:34: When Jephthah came to Mizpah to his house, behold, his daughter was coming out to meet him with timbrels and dancing! And she was his only child; besides her he had neither son nor daughter.
verses.11:35: And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he tore his garments and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you have become one of those who trouble me! For I have opened my mouth to the LORD, and I cannot turn back."
verses.11:36: And she said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD; do to me according to what has gone forth from your mouth, since the LORD has executed vengeance for you upon your enemies, the children of Ammon."
verses.11:37: Then she said to her father, "Let this thing be done for me: leave me alone for two months, that I may go and wander upon the mountains and weep for my virginity, I and my companions."
verses.11:38: And he said, "Go." So he sent her away for two months; and she went with her companions and wept for her virginity upon the mountains.
verses.11:39: And it came to pass at the end of two months that she returned to her father, and he did to her according to his vow which he had vowed; and she had not known a man. And it became a custom in Israel:
verses.11:40: that from year to year the daughters of Israel would go to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in the year.
verses.12:1: Then the men of Ephraim were summoned together, and crossed over to Zaphon; and they said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight against the children of Ammon, and did not call us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire."
verses.12:2: And Jephthah said to them, "I and my people were in fierce contention with the children of Ammon; and when I cried out to you, you did not deliver me from their hand.
verses.12:3: So when I saw that you would not bring deliverance, I took my life in my own hands and crossed over against the children of Ammon, and the LORD gave them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me this day to fight against me?"
verses.12:4: Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim; and the men of Gilead struck down Ephraim, because they had said, "You are fugitives of Ephraim, O Gilead, in the midst of Ephraim and in the midst of Manasseh."
verses.12:5: And Gilead seized the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim. And it came to pass, whenever any of the fugitives of Ephraim said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead would say to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he would say, "No."
verses.12:6: Then they would say to him, "Say now, 'Shibboleth!'" And he would say, "Sibboleth," for he was not able to pronounce it rightly. Then they would seize him and slay him at the fords of the Jordan. And there fell at that time of Ephraim forty-two thousand.
verses.12:7: And Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.
verses.12:8: And after him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.
verses.12:9: He had thirty sons; and thirty daughters he sent outside in marriage, and thirty daughters he brought in from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel seven years.
verses.12:10: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.
verses.12:11: And after him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.
verses.12:12: And Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
verses.12:13: And after him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
verses.12:14: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy young donkeys. And he judged Israel eight years.
verses.12:15: Then Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
verses.13:1: Again the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
verses.13:2: Now there was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren and had borne no children.
verses.13:3: And the Angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "Behold now, you are barren and have borne no children, yet you shall conceive and bear a son.
verses.13:4: Now therefore, take heed, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean.
verses.13:5: For behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. No razor shall come upon his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb; and he shall begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.13:6: Then the woman came and spoke to her husband, saying, "A man of God came to me, and His countenance was like the countenance of the Angel of God, exceedingly awesome; I did not ask Him where He was from, nor did He tell me His name.
verses.13:7: And He said to me, 'Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son. Now therefore, do not drink wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.'"
verses.13:8: Then Manoah prayed to the LORD and said, "O my Lord, please let the man of God whom You sent come to us again and teach us what we shall do for the child who will be born."
verses.13:9: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the Angel of God came again to the woman as she sat in the field; but Manoah her husband was not with her.
verses.13:10: Then the woman made haste and ran and told her husband, and said to him, "Behold, the man who came to me the other day has appeared to me!"
verses.13:11: So Manoah arose and followed his wife. When he came to the man, he said to Him, "Are You the man who spoke to the woman?" And He said, "I am."
verses.13:12: And Manoah said, "Now let Your words come to pass! What shall be the rule of life for the child, and what shall be his work?"
verses.13:13: And the Angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Of all that I said to the woman let her be careful.
verses.13:14: She shall not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, nor let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean. All that I commanded her she shall observe."
verses.13:15: Then Manoah said to the Angel of the LORD, "Please let us detain You, that we may prepare a young goat for You."
verses.13:16: And the Angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Though you detain Me, I will not eat of your food; yet if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." For Manoah did not know that He was the Angel of the LORD.
verses.13:17: Then Manoah said to the Angel of the LORD, "What is Your name, so that when Your word comes to pass we may honor You?"
verses.13:18: And the Angel of the LORD said to him, "Why do you ask My name, seeing it is wonderful?"
verses.13:19: So Manoah took the young goat together with the grain offering, and offered it upon the rock to the LORD. And He did wondrously while Manoah and his wife looked on.
verses.13:20: For it came to pass, as the flame went up toward heaven from off the altar, that the Angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. And Manoah and his wife saw it, and they fell on their faces to the ground.
verses.13:21: And the Angel of the LORD appeared no more to Manoah and to his wife. Then Manoah knew that He was the Angel of the LORD.
verses.13:22: And Manoah said to his wife, "We shall surely die, because we have seen God!"
verses.13:23: But his wife said to him, "If the LORD had desired to put us to death, He would not have received a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hand, nor would He have shown us all these things, nor would He at this time have declared to us such things as these."
verses.13:24: So the woman bore a son and called his name Samson; and the child grew, and the LORD blessed him.
verses.13:25: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.14:1: Now Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.
verses.14:2: So he came up and told his father and his mother, and said, "I have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines; now therefore, get her for me as a wife."
verses.14:3: Then his father and his mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your brethren, or among all my people, that you must go to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" And Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes."
verses.14:4: Now his father and his mother did not know that it was from the LORD, for He was seeking an occasion against the Philistines; for at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
verses.14:5: So Samson went down to Timnah with his father and his mother, and they came to the vineyards of Timnah; and behold, a young lion came roaring against him.
verses.14:6: And the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he tore it apart as one tears a young goat, though he had nothing in his hand. Yet he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.
verses.14:7: Then he went down and spoke to the woman; and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
verses.14:8: And after some days he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion; and behold, a swarm of bees and honey were in the body of the lion.
verses.14:9: So he scraped it out into his hands and went on, eating as he walked. And he came to his father and his mother, and gave some to them, and they ate; yet he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey out of the carcass of the lion.
verses.14:10: Then his father went down to the woman. And Samson made a feast there, for so the young men used to do.
verses.14:11: And it came to pass, when they saw him, that they brought thirty companions to be with him.
verses.14:12: Then Samson said to them, "Let me now pose a riddle to you: if you can surely declare its meaning to me within the seven days of the feast and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.
verses.14:13: But if you cannot declare it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing." And they said to him, "Pose your riddle, that we may hear it."
verses.14:14: So he said to them, "Out of the eater came forth food, and out of the strong came forth sweetness." And for three days they could not explain the riddle.
verses.14:15: And it came to pass on the seventh day that they said to Samson's wife, "Entice your husband, that he may explain the riddle to us, lest we burn you and your father's house with fire. Have you invited us to impoverish us? Is it not so?"
verses.14:16: Then Samson's wife wept upon him and said, "You only hate me and do not love me! You have posed a riddle to the sons of my people, and have not explained it to me." And he said to her, "Behold, I have not explained it to my father or to my mother; shall I then explain it to you?"
verses.14:17: Now she wept before him during the seven days that their feast lasted. And it came to pass on the seventh day that he explained it to her, because she pressed him sorely; and she explained the riddle to the sons of her people.
verses.14:18: So the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, "What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them, "If you had not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found out my riddle!"
verses.14:19: Then the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty of their men, took their spoil, and gave the changes of clothing to those who had explained the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father's house.
verses.14:20: And Samson's wife was given to his companion, who had been his friend.
verses.15:1: Now it came to pass after a time, in the days of the wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a young goat, and he said, "I will go in to my wife, into the inner chamber." Yet her father would not permit him to go in.
verses.15:2: And her father said, "I surely thought that you utterly hated her; therefore I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister fairer than she? Please let her be yours instead of her."
verses.15:3: Then Samson said to them, "This time I am blameless toward the Philistines when I do them harm."
verses.15:4: So Samson went and caught three hundred foxes; and he took torches, turned them tail to tail, and set one torch in the midst between the two tails.
verses.15:5: And he kindled fire in the torches and loosed them into the standing grain of the Philistines, and he burned from the stacked sheaves even to the standing grain, and even to the olive groves.
verses.15:6: Then the Philistines said, "Who has done this?" And they answered, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.
verses.15:7: And Samson said to them, "If this is how you act, I will surely take vengeance upon you, and afterward I will cease."
verses.15:8: So he struck them hip and thigh with a great slaughter; then he went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
verses.15:9: Then the Philistines went up and encamped in Judah, and spread themselves out in Lehi.
verses.15:10: And the men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" So they replied, "We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he has done to us."
verses.15:11: Then three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam, and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us? What is this that you have done to us?" And he said to them, "As they did to me, so have I done to them."
verses.15:12: And they said to him, "We have come down to bind you, that we may deliver you into the hand of the Philistines." And Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you yourselves will not fall upon me."
verses.15:13: So they spoke to him, saying, "No, for we will surely bind you and deliver you into their hand; but we will certainly not put you to death." And they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.
verses.15:14: When he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted as they came to meet him. Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed mightily upon him, and the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that has burned with fire, and his bonds melted away from his hands.
verses.15:15: He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, stretched out his hand and took it, and struck down one thousand men with it.
verses.15:16: Then Samson said, "With the jawbone of a donkey, heaps upon heaps, with the jawbone of a donkey I have struck down one thousand men!"
verses.15:17: And it came to pass, when he had finished speaking, that he cast the jawbone from his hand and named that place Ramath Lehi.
verses.15:18: Then he became exceedingly thirsty, and he cried out to the LORD and said, "You have granted this great deliverance by the hand of Your servant; and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"
verses.15:19: So God split open the hollow place that is in Lehi, and water came forth from it; and when he drank, his spirit returned and he revived. Therefore he called its name En Hakkore, which is in Lehi to this day.
verses.15:20: And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.
verses.16:1: Now Samson went to Gaza and saw a harlot there, and he went in to her.
verses.16:2: Word came to the Gazites, saying, "Samson has come here." So they surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the gate of the city. They kept silent all night, saying, "Wait until the light of morning; then we will slay him."
verses.16:3: And Samson lay until midnight; then he arose at midnight, took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two gateposts, pulled them up together with the bar, laid them upon his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron.
verses.16:4: And it came to pass afterward that he loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.
verses.16:5: Then the lords of the Philistines came up to her and said to her, "Entice him, and see where his great strength lies, and by what means we may prevail against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and each one of us will give you one thousand one hundred pieces of silver."
verses.16:6: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me where your great strength lies, and with what you may be bound to afflict you."
verses.16:7: And Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, then I shall become weak and be like any other man."
verses.16:8: So the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.
verses.16:9: Now men lying in ambush were waiting with her in the inner chamber. And she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" Yet he snapped the bowstrings as a strand of tow snaps when it scents fire. So his strength was not made known.
verses.16:10: Then Delilah said to Samson, "Behold, you have mocked me and spoken lies to me. Now please tell me with what you may be bound."
verses.16:11: And he said to her, "If they securely bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I shall become weak and be like any other man."
verses.16:12: Therefore Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And the men in ambush were waiting in the inner chamber. Yet he snapped them off his arms like a thread.
verses.16:13: Then Delilah said to Samson, "Until now you have mocked me and spoken lies to me. Tell me with what you may be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven locks of my head into the web of the loom."
verses.16:14: And she fastened it tightly with the pin, and said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" And he awoke from his sleep and pulled out the pin of the loom along with the web.
verses.16:15: Then she said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? These three times you have mocked me, and you have not told me where your great strength lies."
verses.16:16: And it came to pass, because she pressed him with her words day after day and urged him, that his soul was vexed to the point of death.
verses.16:17: So he told her all his heart, and said to her, "No razor has ever come upon my head, for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother's womb. If I am shaved, then my strength will depart from me, and I shall become weak and be like all other men."
verses.16:18: When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and summoned the lords of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart." So the lords of the Philistines came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.
verses.16:19: Then she lulled him to sleep upon her knees, and called for a man and had him shave off the seven locks of his head. Then she began to afflict him, and his strength departed from him.
verses.16:20: And she said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" So he awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times and shake myself free." Yet he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
verses.16:21: Then the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes; and they brought him down to Gaza, bound him with bronze fetters, and he became a grinder in the prison house.
verses.16:22: Yet the hair of his head began to grow again after he had been shaved.
verses.16:23: Now the lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god, and to rejoice; and they said, "Our god has delivered into our hand Samson our enemy!"
verses.16:24: And when the people saw him, they praised their god, for they said, "Our god has delivered into our hand our enemy, the destroyer of our land, and the one who has multiplied our slain!"
verses.16:25: And it came to pass, when their hearts were merry, that they said, "Summon Samson, that he may make sport for us." So they summoned Samson from the prison house, and he made sport before them; and they stationed him between the pillars.
verses.16:26: Then Samson said to the lad who held him by the hand, "Let me alone, and let me feel the pillars upon which the house rests, that I may lean against them."
verses.16:27: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and upon the roof were about three thousand men and women watching while Samson made sport.
verses.16:28: Then Samson called to the LORD and said, "O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray, and strengthen me, I pray, just this once, O God, that I may take vengeance at one stroke upon the Philistines for my two eyes!"
verses.16:29: And Samson grasped the two middle pillars upon which the house rested, and he braced himself against them, one with his right hand and the other with his left.
verses.16:30: Then Samson said, "Let my soul die with the Philistines!" And he bowed himself with might, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people who were in it. So the dead whom he slew in his death were more numerous than those whom he had slain in his life.
