verses.16:31: Then his brethren and all the house of his father went down and carried him up, and they buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. Now he had judged Israel twenty years.
verses.17:1: Now there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, whose name was Micah.
verses.17:2: And he said to his mother, "The one thousand one hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse and also spoke in my hearing—behold, the silver is with me; I took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the LORD!"
verses.17:3: So he restored the one thousand one hundred pieces of silver to his mother. Then his mother said, "I have wholly consecrated the silver to the LORD from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a molten image; now therefore I will restore it to you."
verses.17:4: Thus he restored the silver to his mother. And his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to the silversmith, and he made of it a carved image and a molten image; and it was in the house of Micah.
verses.17:5: Now the man Micah had a house of gods, and he made an ephod and household idols, and consecrated one of his sons, who became his priest.
verses.17:6: In those days there was no king in Israel; each man did that which was right in his own eyes.
verses.17:7: Now there was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the clan of Judah; he was a Levite, and he sojourned there.
verses.17:8: And the man departed from the city, from Bethlehem in Judah, to sojourn wherever he might find a place; and as he made his journey, he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah.
verses.17:9: And Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" And he said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I may find a place."
verses.17:10: Then Micah said to him, "Dwell with me, and be to me a father and a priest, and I will give you ten pieces of silver by the year, a suit of apparel, and your sustenance." So the Levite went in.
verses.17:11: And the Levite was content to dwell with the man; and the young man became to him like one of his own sons.
verses.17:12: So Micah consecrated the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and he remained in the house of Micah.
verses.17:13: Then Micah said, "Now I know that the LORD will do good to me, because the Levite has become my priest."
verses.18:1: In those days there was no king in Israel; and in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance for itself to dwell in, for until that day nothing had fallen to it among the tribes of Israel as an inheritance.
verses.18:2: And the children of Dan sent from their clan five men from their whole number, men of valor from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it. And they said to them, "Go, explore the land." So they came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and lodged there.
verses.18:3: While they were by the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? And what are you doing in this place? And what do you have here?"
verses.18:4: And he said to them, "Thus and thus has Micah done for me; he has hired me, and I have become a priest to him."
verses.18:5: And they said to him, "Please inquire of God, that we may know whether our way on which we are going will prosper."
verses.18:6: And the priest said to them, "Go in peace. Your way in which you are going is before the LORD."
verses.18:7: Then the five men went and came to Laish, and they saw the people who were in its midst, dwelling securely after the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting; and there was no one in the land possessing dominion to put them to shame in anything. Moreover, they were far from the Sidonians, and they had no dealings with anyone.
verses.18:8: And they came back to their brethren at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brethren said to them, "What do you say?"
verses.18:9: And they said, "Arise, and let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and behold, it is exceedingly good. And are you keeping still? Do not be slothful in going to enter and possess the land.
verses.18:10: When you go, you will come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is spacious; for God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."
verses.18:11: So six hundred men of the clan of the Danites set out from there, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, girded with weapons of war.
verses.18:12: And they went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they have called that place Mahaneh-dan to this day; behold, it is behind Kiriath-jearim.
verses.18:13: And they passed from there to the hill country of Ephraim, and came to the house of Micah.
verses.18:14: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish answered and said to their brethren, "Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a molten image? Now therefore, consider what you should do."
verses.18:15: So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and inquired of his welfare.
verses.18:16: Now the six hundred men girded with their weapons of war, who were of the children of Dan, stood at the entrance of the gate.
verses.18:17: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up, entered there, and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten image, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men who were girded with weapons of war.
verses.18:18: When these went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the molten image, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
verses.18:19: And they said to him, "Be silent! Put your hand over your mouth, and come with us, and be to us a father and a priest. Is it better for you to be a priest to the household of one man, or to be a priest to a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
verses.18:20: So the priest's heart was glad; and he took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved image, and went into the midst of the people.
verses.18:21: Then they turned and departed, and placed the little ones, the livestock, and the goods before them.
verses.18:22: When they had gone a distance from the house of Micah, the men who were in the houses near Micah's house were gathered together and overtook the children of Dan.
verses.18:23: And they called out to the children of Dan, who turned their faces around and said to Micah, "What ails you, that you have gathered a company?"
verses.18:24: And he said, "You have taken away my gods which I made, and the priest, and have departed! Now what more do I have? How then can you say to me, 'What ails you?'"
verses.18:25: And the children of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, lest men bitter of soul fall upon you, and you lose your life and the lives of your household."
verses.18:26: So the children of Dan went their way. And when Micah saw that they were stronger than he, he turned around and went back to his house.
verses.18:27: And they took the things which Micah had made, and the priest who had belonged to him, and they came against Laish, against a quiet and unsuspecting people; and they struck them with the edge of the sword and burned the city with fire.
verses.18:28: And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon, and they had no dealings with anyone; and it was in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. Then they rebuilt the city and dwelt in it.
verses.18:29: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; however, the name of the city at the first was Laish.
verses.18:30: And the children of Dan set up the carved image for themselves; and Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day of the captivity of the land.
verses.18:31: So they set up for themselves Micah's carved image which he had made, all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh.
verses.19:1: And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a certain Levite sojourning in the remote parts of the hill country of Ephraim. And he took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.
verses.19:2: And his concubine played the harlot against him, and went away from him to her father's house, to Bethlehem in Judah, and was there for four whole months.
verses.19:3: Then her husband arose and went after her, to speak tenderly to her and to bring her back, having his servant and a pair of donkeys with him. And she brought him into her father's house; and when the father of the young woman saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
verses.19:4: So his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, detained him, and he remained with him three days. And they ate and drank, and lodged there.
verses.19:5: And it came to pass on the fourth day that they arose early in the morning, and he rose up to depart; but the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "Refresh your heart with a morsel of bread, and afterward you may go."
verses.19:6: So they sat down, and the two of them ate and drank together. Then the father of the young woman said to the man, "Please consent to stay the night, and let your heart be glad."
verses.19:7: And when the man rose up to depart, his father-in-law urged him strongly, so he turned back and lodged there again.
verses.19:8: And he arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart, and the father of the young woman said, "Please refresh your heart, and tarry until the day declines." So the two of them ate.
verses.19:9: Then the man rose up to depart, he and his concubine and his servant. And his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, "Behold now, the day has drawn toward evening; please lodge for the night. Behold, the day is coming to an end; lodge here, and let your heart be glad, and tomorrow you shall rise early for your journey and go to your tent."
verses.19:10: Yet the man was not willing to lodge for the night; so he rose up and departed, and came opposite Jebus, that is, Jerusalem. With him were a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
verses.19:11: When they were near Jebus, and the day was far spent, the servant said to his master, "Come, please, and let us turn aside into this city of the Jebusites and lodge in it."
verses.19:12: And his master said to him, "We will not turn aside into a city of foreigners, who are not of the children of Israel; rather, we will pass on to Gibeah."
verses.19:13: And he said to his servant, "Come, and let us draw near to one of these places, and we will lodge in Gibeah or in Ramah."
verses.19:14: So they passed on and went their way; and the sun went down on them beside Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
verses.19:15: And they turned aside there to go in and lodge in Gibeah. And he entered and sat down in the open square of the city, for there was no man who took them into his house to lodge.
verses.19:16: And behold, an old man was coming from his work out of the field at evening. Now the man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he was sojourning in Gibeah; whereas the men of the place were Benjaminites.
verses.19:17: And when he lifted up his eyes and saw the traveler in the open square of the city, the old man said, "Where are you going, and from where do you come?"
verses.19:18: And he said to him, "We are passing from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote parts of the hill country of Ephraim; I am from there. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, and now I am going to the house of the LORD; yet there is no man who takes me into his house.
verses.19:19: Moreover, there is both straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine as well for me, for your maidservant, and for the young man who is with your servants; there is no lack of anything."
verses.19:20: And the old man said, "Peace be to you! Only let all your needs be upon me; only do not lodge in the open square."
verses.19:21: So he brought him into his house and gave fodder to the donkeys; and they washed their feet, and ate and drank.
verses.19:22: While they were making their hearts glad, behold, the men of the city, worthless men, surrounded the house, beating on the door; and they spoke to the old man, the master of the house, saying, "Bring out the man who came into your house, that we may know him."
verses.19:23: And the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, "No, my brethren! Please do not act so wickedly! Seeing that this man has come into my house, do not commit this outrageous folly.
verses.19:24: Behold, here are my virgin daughter and his concubine; let me bring them out now, and humble them and do to them whatever seems good in your eyes; but against this man do not commit such an outrageous folly."
verses.19:25: But the men would not listen to him. So the man seized his concubine and brought her out to them; and they knew her and abused her all night until the morning, and they let her go as the dawn broke.
verses.19:26: Then the woman came as morning appeared, and fell down at the entrance of the man's house where her master was, until it was light.
verses.19:27: When her master arose in the morning and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go on his way, behold, the woman, his concubine, was fallen at the entrance of the house with her hands upon the threshold.
verses.19:28: And he said to her, "Arise, and let us go." But there was no answer. So he lifted her onto the donkey, and the man rose up and went to his place.
verses.19:29: And when he entered his house, he took a knife, laid hold of his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel.
verses.19:30: And it came to pass that all who saw it said, "Nothing like this has ever happened or been seen from the day the children of Israel came up from the land of Egypt until this day! Consider it, take counsel, and speak out!"
verses.20:1: Then all the children of Israel went forth, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land of Gilead, to the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.20:2: And the leaders of all the people, of all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand men on foot who drew the sword.
verses.20:3: Now the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel had gone up to Mizpah. And the children of Israel said, "Speak, how did this evil come to pass?"
verses.20:4: So the Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, "I came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to lodge for the night.
verses.20:5: And the men of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house by night because of me; they intended to kill me, and they violated my concubine so that she died.
verses.20:6: So I took hold of my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of the inheritance of Israel, for they have committed depravity and outrage in Israel.
verses.20:7: Behold, all of you are children of Israel; give your word and counsel here."
verses.20:8: Then all the people arose as one man, saying, "Not one of us will go to his tent, nor will any of us return to his house.
verses.20:9: But now this is the thing that we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it by lot.
verses.20:10: We will take ten men out of a hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to bring provisions for the people, so that when they come to Geba of Benjamin, they may repay them according to all the outrage that they have committed in Israel."
verses.20:11: So all the men of Israel gathered against the city, united together as one man.
verses.20:12: Then the tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the clans of Benjamin, saying, "What is this evil that has been done among you?
verses.20:13: Now therefore, deliver up the men, the sons of Belial, who are in Gibeah, that we may put them to death and purge evil from Israel." But the children of Benjamin would not listen to the voice of their brethren, the children of Israel.
verses.20:14: Instead, the children of Benjamin assembled from the cities to Gibeah to go out to battle against the children of Israel.
verses.20:15: And from the cities the children of Benjamin were mustered on that day twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, of whom seven hundred chosen men were mustered.
verses.20:16: Among all this people were seven hundred chosen men who were left-handed; every one of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
verses.20:17: Now the men of Israel, apart from Benjamin, were mustered at four hundred thousand men who drew the sword; all of these were men of war.
verses.20:18: Then they arose, went up to Bethel, and inquired of God. And the children of Israel said, "Who shall go up first for us to battle against the children of Benjamin?" And the LORD said, "Judah first."
verses.20:19: So the children of Israel arose in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.
verses.20:20: And the men of Israel marched out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel set themselves in battle array against them at Gibeah.
verses.20:21: Then the children of Benjamin came forth from Gibeah and struck down to the ground twenty-two thousand men of Israel on that day.
verses.20:22: Yet the people, the men of Israel, took courage and again drew up in battle array at the place where they had arrayed themselves on the first day.
verses.20:23: Then the children of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until evening; and they inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the children of my brother Benjamin?" And the LORD said, "Go up against him."
verses.20:24: So the children of Israel advanced against the children of Benjamin on the second day.
verses.20:25: And Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them on the second day, and struck down to the ground another eighteen thousand men of the children of Israel; all of these drew the sword.
verses.20:26: Then all the children of Israel, and all the people, went up and came to Bethel; they wept and sat there before the LORD, and fasted on that day until evening, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
verses.20:27: And the children of Israel inquired of the LORD—for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,
verses.20:28: and Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days—saying, "Shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of my brother Benjamin, or shall I cease?" And the LORD said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver him into your hand."
verses.20:29: So Israel set men in ambush all around Gibeah.
verses.20:30: And the children of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day and arrayed themselves against Gibeah as at the other times.
verses.20:31: And the children of Benjamin came out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city. They began to strike down some of the people as at the other times, along the highways—one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah—and in the open field, about thirty men of Israel.
verses.20:32: And the children of Benjamin said, "They are routed before us, as at the first." But the children of Israel had said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways."
verses.20:33: Then all the men of Israel rose up from their place and drew up in array at Baal Tamar, while the ambush of Israel burst forth from its place, from the open ground of Geba.
verses.20:34: And ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came opposite Gibeah, and the battle grew fierce; yet they did not know that calamity was closing in upon them.
verses.20:35: And the LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel; and the children of Israel struck down twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin on that day; all of these drew the sword.
verses.20:36: So the children of Benjamin saw that they were defeated. Now the men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, because they trusted in the ambush which they had set against Gibeah.
verses.20:37: And the men in ambush hurried and rushed upon Gibeah; the ambush spread out and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword.
verses.20:38: Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the ambush was that they should cause a great cloud of smoke to rise up from the city.
verses.20:39: Then the men of Israel turned about in the battle. Now Benjamin had begun to strike down and slay about thirty of the men of Israel, for they said, "Surely they are completely defeated before us, as in the first battle."
verses.20:40: But when the signal began to ascend from the city in a pillar of smoke, Benjamin looked behind him, and behold, the whole city was ascending toward heaven.
verses.20:41: And the men of Israel turned around, and the men of Benjamin were dismayed, for they saw that calamity had come upon them.
verses.20:42: Therefore they turned their backs before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, yet the battle overtook them; and those who came out of the cities were destroying them in their midst.
verses.20:43: They surrounded Benjamin, pursued them, and trod them down at their resting place, as far as opposite Gibeah toward the rising of the sun.
verses.20:44: And eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell; all of these were men of valor.
verses.20:45: Then they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, yet the men of Israel gleaned five thousand of them along the highways, and pursued closely after them as far as Gidom, and struck down two thousand men of them.
verses.20:46: So all those of Benjamin who fell on that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword; all of these were men of valor.
verses.20:47: But six hundred men turned and fled into the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and dwelt at the rock of Rimmon for four months.
verses.20:48: And the men of Israel turned back against the children of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from every entire city to the beasts, even everything that was found; moreover, they set fire to all the cities that were found.
verses.21:1: Now the men of Israel had sworn in Mizpah, saying, "No man among us shall give his daughter to Benjamin for a wife."
verses.21:2: And the people came to Bethel and sat there until evening before God, and they lifted up their voice and wept with great weeping.
verses.21:3: And they said, "O LORD, God of Israel, why has this happened in Israel, that one tribe should be missing from Israel this day?"
verses.21:4: And it came to pass on the next day that the people rose early, built an altar there, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings.
verses.21:5: And the children of Israel said, "Who among all the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD in the assembly?" For a great oath had been taken concerning whoever did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah, saying, "He shall surely be put to death."
verses.21:6: And the children of Israel were grieved for Benjamin their brother, and said, "One tribe has been cut off from Israel this day.
verses.21:7: What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters as wives?"
verses.21:8: And they said, "Which one from the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah?" And behold, no man had come to the camp from Jabesh Gilead, to the assembly.
verses.21:9: And the people were mustered, and behold, not one man of the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead was there.
verses.21:10: So the congregation sent there twelve thousand of the men of valor, and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead with the edge of the sword, along with the women and the little ones.
verses.21:11: And this is the thing that you shall do: every male, and every woman who has known lying with a male, you shall devote to utter destruction."
verses.21:12: And they found among the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead four hundred young virgins who had not known a man by lying with a male; and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
verses.21:13: Then the whole congregation sent word and spoke to the children of Benjamin who were at the Rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them.
verses.21:14: So Benjamin returned at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had spared alive from the women of Jabesh Gilead; yet even so there were not enough for them.
verses.21:15: And the people grieved for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
verses.21:16: Then the elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for wives for those who remain, for the women have been destroyed out of Benjamin?"
verses.21:17: And they said, "There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe may not be blotted out from Israel.
verses.21:18: Yet we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the children of Israel have sworn, saying, 'Cursed is he who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"
verses.21:19: Then they said, "Behold, there is a feast of the LORD in Shiloh from year to year, which is on the north of Bethel, on the east side of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and on the south of Lebonah."
verses.21:20: So they commanded the children of Benjamin, saying, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,
verses.21:21: and watch; and behold, when the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out of the vineyards, and let every man seize his wife for himself from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.21:22: And it shall be, when their fathers or their brethren come to us to contend, that we will say to them, 'Graciously grant them to us, because we did not take a wife for each man in the war, and because it was not you who gave them to them, otherwise you would now be guilty.'"
verses.21:23: And the children of Benjamin did so, and took wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they carried off; then they went and returned to their inheritance, and rebuilt the cities and dwelt in them.
verses.21:24: So the children of Israel departed from there at that time, every man to his tribe and to his family, and they went out from there, every man to his inheritance.
verses.21:25: In those days there was no king in Israel; each man would do what was right in his eyes.

notes.1:17: Hormah means "destruction" or "devoted to destruction," echoing the Hebrew verb translated "devoted it to destruction."
notes.1:27: The Hebrew reading tradition (Qere) reads the plural "the inhabitants of Dor," matching the following clauses, whereas the written consonantal text (Ketiv) has the collective singular "the inhabitant of."
notes.1:36: Sela literally means "the Rock" in Hebrew, denoting a prominent geographical landmark along the southern frontier.
notes.2:1: Bochim means "Weepers" in Hebrew, anticipating the people's weeping at that place in verses 4-5.
notes.2:3: The Hebrew word translated "adversaries" can also mean "sides," which traditional renderings often expand as "thorns in your sides" in light of Numbers 33:55.
notes.2:9: Timnath Heres is an alternate form of Timnath Serah (Joshua 24:30), with the consonants of the second element transposed.
notes.2:16: The Hebrew term translated "judges" denotes divinely appointed deliverers and rulers who rescued and governed Israel rather than solely judicial magistrates.
notes.3:8: Aram Naharaim literally means Aram of the Two Rivers, that is, Mesopotamia; the name Cushan-Rishathaim means Cushan of Double Wickedness.
notes.3:15: The Hebrew expression for left-handed literally means bound or restricted in his right hand, forming wordplay with Benjamite, meaning son of the right hand.
notes.3:16: The Hebrew measure gomed occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and denotes a short cubit, approximately eighteen inches.
notes.3:22: The Hebrew word rendered dung occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible; its precise meaning is uncertain, referring either to bodily waste or to the weapon exiting from behind.
notes.3:24: Covering his feet is an idiomatic Hebrew euphemism for relieving oneself.
notes.4:2: Harosheth Hagoyim literally means Harosheth of the Nations.
notes.4:11: The Masoretic Qere reading translates as Zaanannim, whereas the written Ketiv form reads Zaanim.
notes.4:20: The Hebrew command to stand uses an unusual infinitive-like form rather than the standard feminine singular imperative, though Sisera is speaking to Jael.
notes.5:2: The Hebrew phrase rendered "When leaders took the lead" can also be understood as "When locks were unbound," referring to a warrior's vow in battle.
notes.5:5: The verb rendered "flowed" literally denotes flowing or melting, though some take it from a closely related root meaning "quaked."
notes.5:13: The rare poetic verb form here may be read either as "marched down" or as "had dominion."
notes.5:30: The Hebrew literally says "a womb, two wombs," a harsh military idiom referring to captive maidens.
notes.6:5: Ketiv/Qere variant: the written text (ketiv) has the imperfect form "they would come," while the traditional reading (qere), followed here, has "and they would come."
notes.6:15: The Hebrew word rendered "my clan" literally means "my thousand," a term for a tribal subdivision or military unit.
notes.6:34: The Hebrew verb literally means "clothed" or "put on," vividly depicting the Spirit of the LORD enveloping Gideon.
notes.7:3: The Hebrew verb rendered "depart" occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and carries the sense of turning away or hastening back from Mount Gilead.
notes.7:13: The rare Hebrew term for "loaf" denotes a humble round cake of barley bread, symbolizing Gideon's small and lowly band overturning the mighty Midianite camp.
notes.7:21: The Hebrew Ketiv reads a causative form meaning "they put to flight," whereas the Qere followed here reads the simple active form "they fled."
notes.7:25: The names Oreb and Zeeb mean "Raven" and "Wolf," respectively, and the rock and winepress where they were slain bore their names thereafter.
notes.8:13: The Masoretic Hebrew phrase "the Ascent of Heres" names a mountain pass, though some ancient versions understood Heres as a poetic term for the sun.
notes.8:16: The Masoretic Hebrew verb literally means "he caused to know," rendered here "he taught a lesson," referring to severe punishment with the desert thorns and briers threatened in verse seven.
notes.8:26: The Hebrew states the weight simply as "one thousand seven hundred of gold," with the standard unit of shekels understood from the context.
notes.8:33: The name Baal Berith means "Lord of the Covenant," a Canaanite deity worshiped at Shechem.
notes.9:8: The Ketiv writes the fuller spelling מלוכה while the Qere reads the imperative מׇלְכָה, both meaning "Reign!"; the translation follows the Qere.
notes.9:12: The Ketiv writes מלוכי while the Qere reads the feminine imperative מָלְכִי ("reign"); the translation follows the Qere.
notes.9:31: The Hebrew word בְּתׇרְמָה is translated "secretly" (or "craftily"), though some understand it as a place name, "at Tormah" (compare Arumah in verse 41).
notes.9:37: "The center of the land" renders Hebrew טַבּוּר הָאָרֶץ, literally "the navel of the land"; "the Oak of the Diviners" renders אֵלוֹן מְעוֹנְנִים (also transliterated "the Oak of Meonenim").
notes.9:44: "The companies that were with him" preserves the plural noun הָרָאשִׁים of the Masoretic Text for Abimelech's force alongside the other two companies.
notes.10:4: The Hebrew text creates a wordplay between 'donkey colts' and 'towns,' giving both words the same Masoretic vocalization. 'Havoth Jair' means 'the tent-villages of Jair.'
notes.10:11: The Hebrew sentence is elliptical, literally opening 'Not from Egypt...' with the verb 'deliver' implied from the conclusion of the statement in verse twelve.
notes.10:12: The Masoretic Text reads 'Maon,' a people of the southern wilderness; some ancient versions read 'Midian.'
notes.10:16: Literally 'His soul grew short because of the misery of Israel,' a Hebrew idiom expressing deep grief and inability to bear their suffering any longer.
notes.11:24: Chemosh was the national deity of Moab, though Jephthah addresses the king of Ammon here, reflecting the Ammonite claim over formerly Moabite territory north of the Arnon.
notes.11:31: The Hebrew participle translated 'whatever' can denote either 'whatever' or 'whoever,' leaving the exact scope and fulfillment of Jephthah's vow a subject of longstanding discussion.
notes.11:37: The translation follows the Masoretic Qere (read form), 'my companions'; the Ketiv (written form) shows a variant spelling of the same word. The verb rendered 'wander' literally means 'go down.'
notes.11:40: The Hebrew verb translated 'lament' can also mean 'recount' or 'commemorate' (compare Judges 5:11).
notes.12:1: The Hebrew directional form tsaphonah may be rendered either "to Zaphon," a town in Gad in the Jordan Valley (cf. Josh. 13:27), or "northward."
notes.12:6: Shibboleth means "ear of grain" or "flowing stream"; the Ephraimites could not pronounce the initial "sh" sound, betraying their tribal dialect at the Jordan fords.
notes.12:7: Literally "in the cities of Gilead," a Hebrew plural idiom referring to one unspecified city within Gilead.
notes.13:17: The Masoretic Ketiv (written text) reads plural "your words," while the Qere (read text), translated here, reads singular "your word" in agreement with the singular verb.
notes.13:18: The Hebrew word rendered "wonderful" denotes something marvelous and beyond human comprehension, echoed by "did wondrously" in verse 19.
notes.13:25: Mahaneh Dan means "Camp of Dan" (cf. Judg. 18:12), located in the territory between Zorah and Eshtaol.
notes.14:11: The Masoretic Text reads "when they saw him," whereas the Septuagint and Syriac reflect a variant consonant meaning "when they feared him."
notes.14:15: The Masoretic Text reads "on the seventh day"; the Septuagint and Syriac read "on the fourth day," apparently harmonizing with verses 14 and 17.
notes.14:18: The Hebrew uses a rare poetic term for the sun (chares) rather than the common word (shemesh), which shares the same root as Samson's name.
notes.15:5: Hebrew kerem zayit literally means an olive orchard or plantation, rendered here as olive groves.
notes.15:8: Hip and thigh translates the Hebrew idiom leg upon thigh, denoting a thorough and devastating defeat.
notes.15:16: Samson's victory boast plays on the Hebrew word chamor, which means both donkey and heap.
notes.15:19: En Hakkore means Spring of the Caller, recalling Samson's cry to the LORD in his thirst.
notes.16:13: The Masoretic Hebrew leaves Samson's conditional statement abruptly unfinished before Delilah acts in verse fourteen; this translation follows the Masoretic Text without harmonizing to the Septuagint.
notes.16:18: Following the Masoretic Qere (to me) rather than the Ketiv (to her), which preserves direct speech in Delilah's message.
notes.16:21: Prison house translates the Masoretic Qere (house of the bound ones); the Ketiv reads house of the prisoners.
notes.16:25: Follows the Masoretic Qere in both variants: when their hearts were merry (ketiv reads because it was merry) and prison house (house of the bound ones, ketiv prisoners).
notes.16:26: Let me feel follows the Masoretic Qere (from the root for touching or feeling), clarifying the unusual spelling of the Ketiv.
notes.17:1: The Hebrew uses the fuller name Micayehu here and in verse four, and the shortened form Micah from verse five onward; both refer to the same man and are rendered uniformly as Micah.
notes.17:2: Follows the Masoretic Qere for the feminine pronoun you; the Ketiv preserves an archaic Hebrew spelling of the same pronoun.
notes.17:5: Household idols renders Hebrew teraphim, and consecrated translates the Hebrew idiom filled the hand of, used for priestly ordination.
notes.17:10: By the year renders the Hebrew idiom for the days, denoting an annual stipend.
notes.18:7: The Hebrew phrase rendered 'no one in the land possessing dominion to put them to shame in anything' literally describes the absence of any restraining authority or regional magistrate over the isolated city of Laish.
notes.18:14: 'Household idols' translates Hebrew teraphim, small cultic images used in household shrines and divination.
notes.18:30: The Masoretic Text reads 'Manasseh,' traditionally written with a suspended letter nun, reflecting a scribal convention that shielded the name of Moses from association with Danite idolatry.
notes.19:3: Following the Masoretic Qere 'to bring her back'; the written Ketiv reads 'to bring it back' or 'to bring him back.'
notes.19:18: The Masoretic Text reads 'the house of the LORD,' referring to the sanctuary in Shiloh; some ancient versions read 'my house.'
notes.19:21: Following the Masoretic Qere verb form meaning 'gave fodder'; the written Ketiv reflects an orthographic variant of the same verb.
notes.19:25: Following the Masoretic Qere 'as the dawn broke' (literally 'as the rising of the dawn'); the written Ketiv uses the preposition 'at' rather than 'as.'
notes.20:10: The Masoretic Text reads Geba of Benjamin here, used interchangeably with Gibeah of Benjamin in this narrative.
notes.20:13: The qere reads the children of Benjamin, supplying the word for children or sons, whereas the ketiv written text reads simply Benjamin.
notes.20:33: The phrase open ground of Geba renders Hebrew maareh-Geba, literally the bare or open place of Geba, which may also designate a local place name.
notes.20:43: Hebrew menuhah literally means resting place, though it may also be understood adverbially as with ease or as a place name, Menuhah.
notes.20:48: The phrase every entire city follows the Masoretic vocalization ir metom, literally a city of completeness, emphasizing the total devastation of the Benjamite towns.
notes.21:14: The Hebrew clause literally reads "and they did not find for them thus," an idiom meaning the four hundred young women from Jabesh Gilead did not suffice for the six hundred surviving Benjaminites.
notes.21:20: Ketiv reads the singular "and he commanded," whereas the Qere followed here reads the plural "and they commanded," agreeing with the elders of the congregation who are speaking.
notes.21:22: Ketiv reads an alternate spelling from the by-form root for contending, while the Qere followed here reads the standard infinitive construct meaning "to contend" or "to complain." The plea "Graciously grant them to us" reflects the Hebrew double-object construction of the verb for showing favor.
notes.21:25: The Hebrew imperfect verb "would do" conveys habitual past action, closing the book of Judges with a refrain highlighting the covenantal disorder before the rise of the monarchy.
